**Claims check**

| Claim | Status |
|---|---|
| "Plastic-Free Tea Bags" (headline) | Allowlisted ("plastic-free") |
| "Our tea bags are plastic-free and home compostable" | Allowlisted (EN 13432 supplier certificate) |
| "Best tea I've ever had" - Emma, Leeds | Unsupported. Not on the allowlist, no source supplied. |

**Problems**

1. **Testimonial.** "Best tea I've ever had" - Emma, Leeds has no source in the policy or this conversation. Policy section 3 bans invented testimonials, and I can't treat a named customer quote as real without proof. It also carries a superlative ("best") that the brand never makes. Remove it. If Emma is a real customer who gave written permission, supply the source and her approved wording, though the "best" phrasing would still conflict with the superlatives rule, so a different quote would be safer.
2. **Landing page consistency.** Any ad claim must also appear on the landing page. The plastic-free and compostable claims are fine, but check the landing page says the same.

**Compliant version**

Headline: Plastic-Free Tea Bags | Description: Our tea bags are plastic-free and home compostable. Free UK delivery on orders over £25.

I did not count characters because no limit was given. Search ad headlines are typically capped at 30 characters, and "Plastic-Free Tea Bags" is 21, so it fits. The description is 76 characters, within the usual 90 limit. Please confirm against your actual limits.

Optional addition if you want social proof: "Rated 4.8 out of 5 from over 1,200 reviews on our website" is allowlisted, though the full wording is long for a description.
